questions.q: A spherical ball is dropped in a long column of a viscous liquid. The speed (v) of the ball as a function of time (t) may be best represented by

When a spherical ball falls in a viscous liquid, viscous drag increases with speed.
Initially acceleration is high, but drag force gradually balances weight.
Hence, the ball approaches a constant terminal velocity asymptotically.
The v-𝑡 curve starts steeply, then flattens out toward a constant value.
Therefore, the correct representation is (2). ✅

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R

Assertion A: When you squeeze one end of a tube to get toothpaste out from the other end, Pascal’s principle is observed.

Reason R: A change in the pressure applied to an enclosed incompressible fluid is transmitted undiminished to every portion of the fluid and to the walls of its container.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is not correct but R is correct
A is correct but R is not correct
Both A and R is correct and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.solution:
Pascal's law states that the pressure in a closed incompressible fluid is transmitted equally in all directions.

The formula for pressure is given by

P=FA

When a toothpaste is squeezed let the pressure transmitted by P. At the mouth of the toothpaste the pressure will also be equal to P due to Pascal's law. The pressure applied to the tube is transmitted equally throughout the toothpaste. When the pressure reaches the open end, it forces toothpaste out through the opening. Hence, both A&R is correct and R is correct explanation for  A.

Angle of contact between oil and water is obtuse i.e., greater than critical angle of contact θc>90°, therefore they do not stick and that's the reason grease/oil stains can not be removed by water wash. 

Thus, both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as

Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R

Assertion A : A spherical body of radius (5 ± 0.1) mm having a particular density is falling through a liquid of constant density. The percentage error in the calculation of its terminal velocity is 4%.

Reason R : The terminal velocity of the spherical body falling through the liquid is inversely proportional to its radius. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.solution:
The terminal velocity is 

VT=29r2gρ-ρ'η
⇒VT∝r2

Differentiating and dividing by VT,

⇒dVTVT=2drr=2×0.15

So, the percentage error is

dVTVT×100=0.25×100=4%

As can be seen the terminal velocity is directly proportional to the square of the radius. Hence A is true but R is false.

options: Both Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> and Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> are false

Given below are two statements: Statement I : When speed of liquid is zero everywhere, pressure difference at any two points depends on equation $P_1-P_2=\rho g\left(h_2-h_1\right)$. Statement II : In ventury tube shown $2 \mathrm{gh}=v_1^2-v_2^2$
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
questions.solution:
Applying Bernoulli's equation $\mathrm{P}_1+\rho \mathrm{gh}_1+\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrm{v}_1^2=\mathrm{P}_2+\rho \mathrm{gh}_2+\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrm{v}_2^2\left[h_1 \& h_2\right.$ are height of point from any reference level] Given $\mathrm{V}_1=\mathrm{V}_2=0$ (for statement-1) $\therefore \mathrm{P}_1-\mathrm{P}_2=\mathrm{g}\left(\mathrm{h}_2-\mathrm{h}_2\right)$
For statement-2 $\mathrm{P}_1+\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrm{v}_1^2=\mathrm{P}_2+\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrm{v}_2^2\begin{aligned} & P_1-P_2=\rho g h \\ & P_1-P_2=\frac{1}{2} \rho v_2^2-\frac{1}{2} \rho v_1^2 \\ & \rho g h=\frac{1}{2} \rho v_2^2-\frac{1}{2} \rho v_1^2 \\ & 2 g h=v_2^2-v_1^2 \end{aligned}$

questions.q:
Statement (A): When the temperature increases the viscosity of gases increases and the viscosity of liquids decreases.

Statement (B): Water does not wet an oily glass because cohesive force of oil is less than that of water.

Statement (C) : A liquid will wet a surface of a solid if the angle of contact is greater than 90°.
options: A. B. and C are false

A and B false,
C is true
B and C false, A is true
A and C false, B is true
questions.solution:
Statement A:

In liquid: With the rise in temperature, viscosity of a liquid decreases because the intermolecular attractive force between consecutive layers decreases as temperature increases. 

In gasses: The important cause of viscosity is randomness/molecular collision due to root mean square velocity. Due to rise in temperature, kinetic energy of molecules increases which makes rms velocity increase, hence randomness and collision of molecules increases. This makes the flow difficult and hence viscosity in gasses increases with temperature.

Statement B:

Water does not wet an oily glass, because  cohesive force for water > adhesive force between water and oil molecules.

Statement C:

When the liquid does not wet the sides of a solid object, it means that the angle of contact is more than 90° but less than 180°.

questions.q:
A tank is filled with a liquid and a small hole is made near the bottom of the tank. Consider the speed \(v\) of efflux of liquid through the hole.
Statements:
1. \(v\) depends on the area of the hole.
2. \(v\) depends on the density of the liquid.
3. \(v\) depends on the height of the liquid column above the hole.
4. \(v\) depends on the acceleration due to gravity.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
We use Torricelli's theorem for efflux speed: \(v=\sqrt{2 g h}\)
- Depends on height (h) of liquid column
- Depends on acceleration due to gravity (g)
- Does NOT depend on area of hole (area affects discharge, not velocity)
- Does NOT depend on density (cancels out in Bernoulli's equation)

questions.q:
A container filled with liquid is placed on a smooth surface. Two points A and B are in same level as shown, state about pressures at these points for following cases, in which container accelerates along given direction
\(\begin{array}{|c|l|c|l|} \hline & \text{Column-A} & & \text{Column-B} \\ \hline (i) & a_x = 0,\; a_y \neq 0 & (A) & P_A = P_B \\ (ii) & a_x = 0,\; a_y = 0 & (B) & P_A > P_B \\ (iii) & a_x > 0,\; a_y = 0 & (C) & P_A < P_B \\ (iv) & a_x > 0,\; a_y > 0 & & \\ \hline \end{array}\)
options: i \(\rightarrow\) B, ii \(\rightarrow\) A, iii \(\rightarrow\) A, iv \(\rightarrow\) B
i \(\rightarrow\) A, ii \(\rightarrow A\), iii \(\rightarrow B\), iv \(\rightarrow B\)
i \(\rightarrow\) A, ii \(\rightarrow\) B, iii \(\rightarrow\) A, iv \(\rightarrow B\)
i \(\rightarrow\) B, ii \(\rightarrow\) A, iii \(\rightarrow\) B, iv \(\rightarrow\) A
questions.solution:
Case (i): \(a_x=0, a_y \neq 0\)
- Vertical acceleration only \(\rightarrow\) pressure distribution changes with depth only, not horizontally.
- So, \(P_A=P_B\).
\(\rightarrow\) Matches A.
Case (ii): \(a_x=0, a_y=0\)
- No acceleration \(\rightarrow\) normal hydrostatic condition.
- Same level \(\Rightarrow\) same pressure.
- So, \(P_A=P_B\).
\(\rightarrow\) Matches A.
Case (iii): \(a_x>0, a_y=0\)
- Accelerating in \(+x \Rightarrow\) pressure increases opposite to acceleration (left side has higher pressure).
- A is on left, B on right \(\Rightarrow P_A>P_B\).
\(\rightarrow\) Matches B.
Case (iv): \(a_x>0, a_y>0\)
- Combined acceleration: vertical affects depth, horizontal affects sidewise pressure.
- At same level, vertical component doesn't matter.
- So, still \(P_A>P_B\).
\(\rightarrow\) Matches B.
